name: Keshi in Search of AmShZ
description: AmShZ has traveled to Italy from Iran for the Thom Yorke concert. There are $$$n$$$ cities in Italy indexed from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ directed roads indexed from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. Initially, Keshi is located in the city $$$1$$$ and wants to go to AmShZ's house in the city $$$n$$$. Since Keshi doesn't know the map of Italy, AmShZ helps him to see each other as soon as possible. In the beginning of each day, AmShZ can send one of the following two messages to Keshi: AmShZ sends the index of one road to Keshi as a blocked road. Then Keshi will understand that he should never use that road and he will remain in his current city for the day. AmShZ tells Keshi to move. Then, Keshi will randomly choose one of the cities reachable from his current city and move there. (city $$$B$$$ is reachable from city $$$A$$$ if there's an out-going road from city $$$A$$$ to city $$$B$$$ which hasn't become blocked yet). If there are no such cities, Keshi will remain in his current city. Note that AmShZ always knows Keshi's current location. AmShZ and Keshi want to find the smallest possible integer $$$d$$$ for which they can make sure that they will see each other after at most $$$d$$$ days. Help them find $$$d$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ $$$(2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5, 1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$  — the number of cities and roads correspondingly. The $$$i$$$-th line of the following $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$v_i$$$ and $$$u_i$$$ $$$(1 \le v_i , u_i \le n,v_i \neq u_i)$$$, denoting a directed road going from city $$$v_i$$$ to city $$$u_i$$$. It is guaranteed that there is at least one route from city $$$1$$$ to city $$$n$$$. Note that there may be more than one road between a pair of cities in each direction.
output_specification: Output the smallest possible integer $$$d$$$ to make sure that AmShZ and Keshi will see each other after at most $$$d$$$ days.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1693C — Keshi in Search of AmShZ [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
